record.title: Universal finite generation for homology of graph configuration spaces
record.statement: Let $F_n(G)$ be the configuration space of $n$ ordered points in a graph $G$. For a class of graphs, universal finite generation in degree $i$ and with $n$ particles means that a finite collection of graphs generates $H_i(F_n(G))$ for every graph in the class via classes arising from topological subgraphs homeomorphic to members of that collection. **Universal finite generation conjecture.** Universal finite generation holds for the class of all graphs. This is the main finiteness conjecture for homology of graph configuration spaces; the paper explains that it would follow from the categorical graph minor and categorical Robertson conjectures, and records supporting results in several special cases.
record.source_name: Ben Knudsen and Eric Ramos, “Robertson's conjecture and universal finite generation in the homology of graph braid groups”, arXiv:2305.19363 (2024).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2305.19363

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of May 2023).

record.title: Boyer et al.'s zero forcing set domination conjecture for paths
record.statement:
Let $G$ be a graph on $n$ vertices, and let $z(G;i)$ denote the number of zero forcing sets of $G$ of size $i$. Let $P_n$ be the path graph on $n$ vertices.

**Boyer et al.'s conjecture.** For every graph $G$ on $n$ vertices,

$$
z(G;i)\leq z(P_n,i)
$$

for all $i\geq 1$.

The conjecture asserts that paths dominate all graphs in the number of zero forcing sets of each positive size. It arises from the counting problem for zero forcing sets, which has been studied for several graph classes; its resolution is not indicated in the supplied text.
record.source_name: Krishna Menon and Anurag Singh, “Exploring the Influence of Graph Operations on Zero Forcing Sets”, arXiv:2405.01423 (2024).

record.title: Blow-up conjecture for inversion diameter
record.statement:
Let $G$ be a graph, let $t$ be a positive integer, let $\overline{K}_t$ be the edgeless graph on $t$ vertices, and let $G[\overline{K}_t]$ denote the blow-up of $G$ in which each vertex is replaced by an independent set of size $t$. Let $\mathcal{I}(G)$ be the inversion graph of $G$. **Blow-up conjecture.** For every graph $G$ and every positive integer $t$,

$$
\operatorname{diam}(\mathcal{I}(G[\overline{K}_t])) \leqslant t\cdot\operatorname{diam}(\mathcal{I}(G)).
$$

The conjecture seeks to generalise the paper's upper bound for complete multipartite graphs to blow-ups of arbitrary graphs.

record.title: Almost-spanning subtree ratio conjecture for the complete graph
record.statement:
Let $G$ be a graph of order $n$. For $1\le k\le n$, let $s_k(G)$ denote the number of subtrees of $G$ with $k$ vertices; in particular, $s_n(G)$ counts spanning trees.

**Almost-spanning subtree ratio conjecture.** For every graph $G$ of order $n$,

$$
s_{n-1}(G)\ge \frac{s_{n-1}(K_n)}{s_n(K_n)}s_n(G).
$$

This is proposed as a reduction toward proving that the complete graph has greatest mean subtree order. Its status is not resolved in the supplied text.
record.source_name: Stijn Cambie, Jorik Jooken and Stephan Wagner, “On the extrema of the mean subtree order of graphs”, arXiv:2508.20593 (2025).

record.title: Verstraëte's conjecture on packing graph subdivisions
record.statement: Given graphs $F$ and $G$, a **subdivision packing** of $F$ in $G$ is a collection of pairwise vertex-disjoint copies of subdivisions of $F$. For a real number $\eta > 0$ and a graph $F$, let $d_0=d_0(F,\eta)$ be a threshold degree. **Verstraëte's conjecture.** For every graph $F$ and every $\eta>0$, there exists $d_0=d_0(F,\eta)$ such that, for every integer $d\ge d_0$, every $d$-regular graph $G$ of order $n$ contains a subdivision packing covering all but at most $\eta n$ vertices of $G$. This conjecture concerns approximate spanning packings in dense regular graphs; the paper establishes stronger perfect-packing results when the degree is linear in the order of the graph.

record.title: Toruńczyk's conjecture on blind flip-width and linear clique-width
record.statement: Let $\mathscr{C}$ be a class of graphs. **Toruńczyk's conjecture.** The class $\mathscr{C}$ has bounded blind flip-width if and only if it has bounded linear clique-width. Toruńczyk introduced blind flip-width as a blind variant of flip-width, motivated by the fact that infinite-radius blind flip-width is functionally equivalent to linear clique-width. The conjecture asks whether boundedness of these parameters is equivalent for every graph class; no resolution is given here.

record.title: S. Akbari, H. Kumar, and B. Mohar's negative $p$-energy conjecture
record.statement:
Let $n$ and $p$ be positive integers with $p\geq 2$, let $G$ be a connected graph on $n$ vertices, and let $K_n$ denote the complete graph on $n$ vertices. **Akbari–Kumar–Mohar's negative $p$-energy conjecture.**

$$
\mathcal{E}_p^-(G)\geq \mathcal{E}_p^-(K_n).
$$

The source states that the conjecture was known for $p\geq 4$ and that this paper proves it for every integer $p\geq 3$; consequently, the remaining case $p=2$ is still open.
record.source_name: Zhengbo Chen, Zhouningxin Wang and Xiao-Dong Zhang, “Positive and negative 3-energies of graphs”, arXiv:2604.15656 (2026).

record.title: Kára–Pór–Wood Big-Line–Big-Clique Conjecture
record.statement: Let $A\subset\mathbb{R}^2$ be a finite planar point set. Two points of $A$ are **visible** if the open segment between them contains no other point of $A$; a mutually visible subset is a set whose pairs are all visible. **Big-Line–Big-Clique Conjecture.** For every pair of integers $k,\ell\ge 2$ there is $n_0(k,\ell)$ such that every set $A\subset\mathbb{R}^2$ with $|A|\ge n_0(k,\ell)$ contains either $k$ collinear points or $\ell$ mutually visible points. This is a Ramsey-type problem for planar point sets. The paper proves the conclusion in several structured regimes, including point sets on fixed irreducible algebraic curves, but the full conjecture remains open.
record.source_name: Sohail Sarkar, “Visibility cliques, cubic containers, and dense orchard cores”, arXiv:2605.00918 (2026).

record.title: Weighted Frankl conjecture for union-closed families
record.statement:
Let $[n]=\{1,\ldots,n\}$, and let $\mathcal{F}\subseteq 2^{[n]}$ be a non-empty **union-closed family**, meaning that $A\cup B\in\mathcal{F}$ for all $A,B\in\mathcal{F}$. Let $x_1,x_2,\ldots,x_n\geq1$ be real numbers. **Weighted Frankl conjecture.** There exists $k\in[n]$ such that

$$
\sum_{S\in\mathcal{F},\ k\in S}\prod_{m\in S,\ m\neq k}x_m\geq\sum_{S\in\mathcal{F},\ k\notin S}\prod_{m\in S}x_m.
$$

This weighted assertion is motivated by blowing up each element into a family of non-empty subsets. The source presents it as a new conjecture derived from Frankl's conjecture, and gives no resolution; in particular, its general validity remains open.
record.source_name: Veronica Phan, “Blow-up trick in Combinatorics”, arXiv:2605.06725 (2026).

record.title: The truncation invariance conjecture for matroid zeta-function coefficients
record.statement:
Let $M$ be a matroid of rank $r>0$, and let $\tr(M)$ denote its truncation. Write $Z^{\top}_M(s)$ for the topological zeta function of $M$.

**Truncation invariance conjecture.** For every integer $k$ with $0\leqslant k<\operatorname{rk}(M)$,

$$
\left(\frac{d^k}{ds^k}Z^{\top}_M(s)\right)\bigg|_{s=0}=\left(\frac{d^k}{ds^k}Z^{\top}_{\tr(M)}(s)\right)\bigg|_{s=0}.
$$

This conjecture generalizes the known result for matroids whose truncation is uniform. A proof would show that the low-order Taylor coefficients of the topological zeta function are controlled by the corresponding truncation and, consequently, by low-rank information in the lattice of flats.

record.title: Ternary-partition numerator conjecture at minus one
record.statement:
Let $\mathcal T(n)$ be the set of ternary partitions of $n$, meaning partitions whose parts are powers of $3$, and define 
$$
s(n)=\mathrm{num}_{\mathcal T}(n,-1).
$$
 **Ternary-partition evaluation conjecture.** One has $s(1)=s(2)=1$ and, for every relevant integer $n$, 
$$
s(3n)=s(3n+1)=s(3n+2)=3^{\mathrm{val}_3((3n)!)}.
$$
 This is one of the open questions proposed for restricted partition sets and remains open.
record.source_name: Cristina Ballantine, George Beck, Brooke Feigon and Kathrin Maurischat, “Reciprocals of Subsum Polynomials”, arXiv:2605.10512 (2026).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.10512

Status: **open** according to the source (as of May 2026). “In Section , we discuss open questions for sums of reciprocals of subsum polynomials defined on restricted sets of partitions.”

record.title: Fu–Peng–Zhang's coloring conjecture for finitary upho posets
record.statement:
An **upho poset** is a poset whose every principal filter is order-isomorphic to the whole poset; it is **finitary** when its intervals are finite. A coloring assigns labels to the covering edges of an upho poset in a way compatible with the principal-filter isomorphisms.

**Fu–Peng–Zhang's coloring conjecture.** Every finitary upho poset, in particular every finite-type $\mathbb{N}$-graded upho poset, has a coloring.

By the equivalence established in the paper, this is equivalent to the corresponding multiplicability statement. The conjecture is disproved by the paper's Petersen-graph construction, which yields a finitary finite-type $\mathbb{N}$-graded upho poset with no coloring.

record.title: Injectivity conjecture for skew Schur partition functions of two-row partitions
record.statement: Let $\lambda'$ be a two-row partition, and let $\mathrm{prs}_{\lambda'}$ be the associated skew Schur partition function, defined on those partitions for which the function is defined. **Two-row skew Schur injectivity conjecture.** For every two-row partition $\lambda'$, the function $\mathrm{prs}_{\lambda'}$ is injective on $\mathcal{P}(n)$ for every positive integer $n$ on which $\mathrm{prs}_{\lambda'}$ is defined. This refines an earlier question about injectivity of these functions; no resolution is given in the supplied text.

record.title: Deficient-score-sequence characterization of complete partitions
record.statement:
Let $\lambda$ be a partition, let $\lambda'\subseteq\lambda$ denote a subpartition in the paper's sense, and let $\mathfrak{S}^2(\lambda')$ be the set of score sequences of $2$-tournaments with shape $\lambda'$. A sequence is **deficient** according to the paper's preceding definition.

**Deficient-sequence characterization conjecture.** A partition $\lambda$ is complete if and only if, for every $\lambda'\subseteq\lambda$, the set $\mathfrak{S}^2(\lambda')$ has no deficient sequences:

$$
\mathfrak{S}^2(\lambda')\text{ has no deficient sequences for all }\lambda'\subseteq\lambda.
$$

The source states that this is equivalent to the complete-partition classification conjecture. The surrounding theorem gives partial implications, but the source gives no resolution of the conjecture.

record.title: Binary path configuration conjecture for avalanche homology
record.statement:
Let $P_n$ be the directed path on $n$ vertices, let $\beta_i$ denote the $i$-th Betti number of its avalanche complex, and let a **binary configuration** be an initial configuration whose entries are all either $0$ or $1$. **Binary path homology conjecture.** If $\mathbf{c}_0$ is a binary configuration, then for $\mathcal{A}(P_n,\mathbf{c}_0)$ we have

$$
\beta_i=0 \quad\text{for all } i>\left\lfloor\frac{n}{2}\right\rfloor-1.
$$

This would identify the configuration in Proposition 1 as having the highest possible degree of homology among binary initial configurations. The conjecture is refuted once the binary condition is relaxed: $\mathcal{A}(P_7,(5,0,1,1,1,1,1))$ has $\beta_4=1$.
record.source_name: Henri Riihimäki and Jason P. Smith, “Avalanche homology of digraphs via sandpile dynamics”, arXiv:2606.26786 (2026).

Status: **refuted** according to the source (as of June 2026).

record.title: Prowse–Woodall $(a:b)$-choosability equivalence conjecture
record.statement: Let $L$ be an $a$-list assignment on a graph $G$. The graph is **$(a:b)$-choosable** when every such assignment admits a choice of a $b$-element sublist at each vertex whose selected lists are disjoint across edges. Let $(G)_b$ denote the graph operation used in the source. **Prowse–Woodall's $(a:b)$-choosability equivalence conjecture.** For all $a,b\in\mathbb{N}$, a graph $G$ is $(a:b)$-choosable if and only if $(G)_b$ is $a$-choosable. The supplied text says this conjecture was disproved by Dvořák et al. using a 4-choosable graph that is not $(8:2)$-choosable.
record.source_name: Nandana K Vasudevan, K Somasundaram and N Narayanan, “List-Coloring and Chromatic-Choosability – A Dynamic Survey”, arXiv:2606.31702 (2026).

record.title: Permutation-module decomposition conjecture for Hessenberg-variety cohomology
record.statement: Let $k$ be a positive integer, let $h\colon [k]\rightarrow [k]$ be a Hessenberg function, let $S$ be a regular semisimple operator on $\mathbb C^k$, and let $\mathfrak S_k$ act on $H^{2d}(\operatorname{Hess}(S,h))$ by Tymoczko's dot action. For a partition $\lambda=(\lambda_1,\ldots,\lambda_\ell)$ of $k$, let $\mathfrak S_\lambda$ be the corresponding Young subgroup and define the permutation module $M^\lambda=\operatorname{Ind}_{\mathfrak S_\lambda}^{\mathfrak S_k}{\bf 1}$. **Permutation-module decomposition conjecture.** For every $d$, the $\mathbb C\mathfrak S_k$-module $H^{2d}(\operatorname{Hess}(S,h))$ is a direct sum of permutation modules $M^\lambda$. This is the representation-theoretic reformulation of the refined Stanley–Stembridge conjecture; its general validity remains open.

record.title: Generalized Pythagorean partition-regularity conjecture
record.statement:
Let $a,b,c\in\mathbb{N}$, and call the equation $ax^2+by^2=cz^2$ **partition regular** when every finite colouring of $\mathbb{N}$ admits a solution $(x,y,z)\in\mathbb{N}^3$ whose three entries have the same colour.

**Generalized Pythagorean partition-regularity conjecture.** The equation

$$
ax^2+by^2=cz^2
$$

is partition regular if and only if $c\in\{a,b,a+b\}$.

Rado's theorem gives the necessity of the condition $c\in\{a,b,a+b\}$, but its sufficiency remains open. Indeed, it is unknown whether any choice of $a,b,c\in\mathbb{N}$ makes this equation partition regular. The paper proves a special case when $a,b,c$ are perfect squares and either $a=c$ or $a+b=c$.

record.title: Path-maximizes analytic spread among trees
record.statement:
Let $T_1$ and $T_2$ be trees on $n$ and $m$ vertices, respectively, and fix $i\in V(T_1)$ and $j\in V(T_2)$. For a positive integer $l$, define $G_1$ as the tree on $n+m+l$ vertices with edge set

$$
E(T_1)\sqcup E(T_2)\sqcup\\{\\{i,m+n+1\\},\\{m+n+1,m+n+2\\},\ldots,\\{m+n+l,j\\}\\},
$$

and define $G_2$ as the tree on $n+m+l$ vertices obtained by identifying $i$ with $j$ in the disjoint union of $T_1$ and $T_2$, then adjoining the tail with edges $\\{i,n+m+1\\},\\{n+m+1,n+m+2\\},\ldots,\\{m+n+l,m+n+l+1\\}$. **Path-maximization conjecture.** For every graph $H$,

$$
\ell(J_{G_1,H})\geq\ell(J_{G_2,H}).
$$

The proposed comparison says that separating the two trees and joining them by a path does not decrease analytic spread relative to identifying the attachment vertices and adding a tail. The source notes that this would imply $\ell(J_{P_n,H})\geq\ell(J_{T,H})$ for every $n$-vertex tree $T$ and every graph $H$, but gives no proof or resolution.

record.title: Theo-Conjecture for connected cographs
record.statement:
Let $G$) be a connected cograph with no universal vertex. For the co-components $H_{(1)}$ and $H_{(2)}$ defined as in Proposition~, **Theo-Conjecture.**

$$
\operatorname{zdmg}(G)=q(H_{(1)})+q(H_{(2)}).
$$

The cograph condition is essential to the proposed extension: in a general join, internal common neighbors may allow a more efficient confinement strategy. Whether the asserted formula holds for all connected cographs remains open.
